extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) responding to or drafting restriction requirements under the MPEP (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when claims in a US patent application are distinct or independent and when a restriction requirement is proper, including criteria for combinations/subcombinations, product/process/appartus relationships, burden-of-proof factors, linking claims, election of species, and rejoinder practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims to a combination and claims to subcombinations are presented together and the combination requires the particulars of at least one subcombination, both two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-way distinctness must be shown (see subsequent relationship-specific tests). Restriction is only proper when there would be a serious burden if restriction were not required, as evidenced by separate classification, status, or field of search (see MPEP § 806.05(c)). Use form paragraphs such as 8.16 for subcombinations. If inability to show two-way distinctness or reasons for burden, restriction should not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombination distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Each subcombination is distinct from the combination as claimed if: (A) the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability (e.g., to show novelty and unobviousness), and (B) the subcombination can be shown to have utility either by itself or in another materially different combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 806.05(c) and form paragraph 8.16. Examiner must show by example that one of the subcombinations has utility other than in the disclosed combination. If applicant elects a subcombination and claims thereto are found allowable, withdrawn claims that depend from or require all limitations of the allowable subcombination will be examined for patentability per 37 CFR 1.104 (MPEP § 821.04). If applicant rebuts examiner's suggested alternate use as impossible/unreasonable, burden shifts to examiner to document a viable alternative use or withdraw the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and apparatus distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A process and apparatus for its practice are distinct if either: (A) the process as claimed can be practiced by another materially different apparatus or by hand; or (B) the apparatus as claimed can be used to practice another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.17 may be used. The examiner bears the burden to provide reasonable examples that recite material differences (the example need not be documented). If applicant proves there is no material difference or that a process cannot be performed by hand (if so argued by examiner), the burden shifts to the examiner to document another materially different process or apparatus or withdraw the requirement. A process can be practiced by hand if it can be performed without using any apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process of making and product made distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A process of making and a product made by the process can be distinct if either: (A) the process as claimed is not an obvious process of making the product and the process can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of different processes or products need not be documented. A product defined by the process by which it can be made is still a product claim (In re Bridgeford). If applicant convincingly traverses the requirement, the burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable alternative process or product, or withdraw the requirement. Use form paragraphs 8.18 and 8.21.04 in such restriction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus and product made distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: An apparatus and a product made by the apparatus are distinct if either: (A) the apparatus as claimed is not an obvious apparatus for making the product and can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different apparatus (MPEP § 806.05(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.19 may be used. Examiner must show by example either that the apparatus is not an obvious apparatus and can make another product, or that the product can be made by a materially different apparatus. The burden is on the examiner to provide an example, but it need not be documented. If applicant proves the alternative example is not workable, examiner must suggest another viable example or withdraw the restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and process of using distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A product and a process of using the product are distinct if either: (A) the process of using as claimed can be practiced with another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be used in a materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 8.20 and 8.21.04 should be used for restriction requirements between product and method of using. The examiner must provide an example (not necessarily documented). If applicant proves the alternative use cannot be accomplished, the burden shifts to the examiner to support a viable alternative use or withdraw the requirement. All restriction requirements between product and process of using should be followed by form paragraph 8.21.04 to notify applicants about potential rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-way situations (product, process of making, process of using)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims to all three categories (product, process of making, and process of use) are included, a three-way requirement for restriction can only be made where the process of making is distinct from the product. If the process of making and the product are not distinct, the process of using may be joined even though distinctness between product and process of using can be shown (MPEP § 806.05(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims include a product, a process specially adapted for making the product (not patentably distinct from making the product), and a process of using, applicant may be required to elect either (A) the product and process of making it; or (B) the process of using. If the examiner cannot show distinctness between the process of using and the product, restriction cannot be required. Use form paragraph 8.20 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related products or related processes distinctness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To support restriction between two or more related product inventions or related process inventions, both two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction are necessary. For related inventions (not combination/subcombination), inventions are distinct if: (A) the inventions as claimed do not overlap in scope (mutually exclusive); (B) the inventions as claimed are not obvious variants; and (C) the inventions as claimed are either not capable of use together or can have a materially different design, mode of operation, function, or effect (MPEP § 806.05(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden is on the examiner to provide an example to support the determination (example need not be documented). Intermediate vs final product example: distinctness if intermediate useful to make other than the final product and species are patentably distinct. See form paragraphs 8.14.01, 8.14 (intermediate-final), and 8.16 (subcombinations) as appropriate. If generic or linking claims are present, see MPEP § 809.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent inventions definition and restriction justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions as claimed are independent if there is no disclosed relationship between the inventions (i.e., they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect). If two or more inventions are independent and there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required, applicant should be required to restrict the claims to one of such independent inventions (MPEP § 806.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: two different combinations not disclosed as capable of use together with different modes of operation, functions, and effects; unrelated process and apparatus where apparatus cannot be used to practice the process. Use form paragraphs 8.20.02 (unrelated inventions) or 8.20.03 (unrelated product and process) as appropriate. Examiner must show serious burden to require restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for insisting upon restriction — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Every requirement to restrict has two aspects: (A) the reasons (not a mere conclusion) why each invention as claimed is either independent or distinct from the other(s); and (B) the reasons why there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required (MPEP § 808).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The particular reasons relied on by the examiner should be concisely stated; a mere statement of conclusion is inadequate. For example, relative to a combination and a subcombination, the examiner should point out why the subcombination has utility by itself or in other combinations and why the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination. Use form paragraphs 8.01, 8.02, and 8.14–8.20.02 as appropriate. When a disclosed relationship between species exists, that relation must be discussed and reasons advanced explaining why it does not prevent restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing examiner's burden (showing serious burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish reasons for insisting upon restriction, the examiner must explain why there would be a serious burden if restriction is not required by showing one of: (A) separate classification thereof; (B) a separate status in the art when classifiable together; or (C) a different field of search (MPEP § 808.02 / 809.02(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate classification shows recognition in the art as a separate subject and separate field of search (patents need not be cited). Separate status in the art can be shown by citing patents as evidence of recognition and separate field of search. A different field of search exists where searching for one invention is unlikely to find art pertinent to the other (different classes/subclasses, electronic resources, different queries). If classification, field of search, and status are the same and no indication of separate future classification exists, no reasons exist for dividing among independent or related inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claims and effect on restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims are claims which, if allowable, would require rejoinder of otherwise divisible inventions (e.g., genus claims linking species, subcombination claims linking plural combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking claims and the inventions they link are usually all products or all processes. Where an application includes distinct inventions and linking claims, restriction can still be required; linking claims must be examined with and considered part of the invention elected. When all claims directed to the elected invention are allowable, any allowable linking claim requires withdrawal of the restriction and rejoining of previously withdrawn claims that depend from or require all limitations of the allowable linking claim. If withdrawn claims were cancelled by applicant, examiner must notify applicant that canceled nonelected claims depending from an allowable linking claim may be reinstated by amendment and then fully examined for patentability (see MPEP § 821.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species — when required and grouping unpatentable species
rubrics_metrics.description: Election of species may be required even prior to a search (A) in applications with a plurality of species and no generic claims, and (B) in applications with both species claims and generic or Markush claims. Election should not be required between claimed species considered clearly unpatentable (obvious) over each other; the examiner should group species considered clearly unpatentable over each other (MPEP § 808.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In applications with only generic claims, restriction cannot be required unless the generic claims encompass such multiplicity of species that an unduly extensive and burdensome search would be necessary. If applicant presents species claims to more than one patentably distinct species after an Office action on only generic claims with no restriction, the Office may require election of a single species for examination. If a generic claim is found allowable, treat the application as indicated in MPEP § 809 and § 821.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder practice (withdrawal of restriction and rejoinder of claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims to elected combination inventions are allowable or if a linking claim becomes allowable, the examiner must reconsider and withdraw the restriction requirement; any subcombinations or non-elected claims that were searched and determined allowable must be rejoined and examined for patentability. In Ochiai/Brouwer situations, notice of potential rejoinder of process claims must be given (form paragraph 8.21.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon allowance of the elected product, withdrawn process claims that depend from or require all limitations of the allowable product claim will be considered for rejoinder; rejoined claims must meet all patentability criteria (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112). Withdrawn process claims not commensurate in scope with an allowable product will not be rejoined. To retain right to rejoinder, applicant should amend process claims to require the limitations of the product claims during prosecution; failure to do so may result in loss of right to rejoinder. The prohibition against double patenting rejections of 35 U.S.C. 121 does not apply where restriction is withdrawn before issue (MPEP § 804.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's burden to provide examples and applicant rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide an example to support a determination that inventions are distinct or that an alternative use/process/apparatus exists; the example need not be documented. If applicant proves or convincingly argues that the examiner's example is not workable, the burden shifts to the examiner to suggest another viable example or withdraw the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule appears in multiple relationship contexts (process/apparatus, apparatus/product, product/process of using, related inventions). Examiner should provide reasonable, concrete examples that recite material differences. Documentation is not required but may be necessary if applicant rebuts the example. Failure to do so should result in withdrawal of the restriction requirement.
